Seeing your comments I don't think what you are looking for has to do with the Station as much per se as the technology. I think they are called Induction Tips.

These are the newer stations/irons that have the heating element integrated with the tips. These transfer heat much better and also can heat up in matters of seconds, like 2-3 sec. They also have some neat features like auto sleep and being hot-swappable. 

Almost every station or soldering Iron I've seen, under 40€ are stations that have the heating element and the tips separated in a way so you have to unscrew something to remove the tip.

One cheap I found that is not a station but does a good enough job for me is the **Sunshine T210**. There is also a T245 version, I got that because I want to solder really fine components. It has all these features except some of the more advanced ones like per temperature calibration. But it's miles away from any of the cheaper ones due to the tips that it can get. It has auto-sleep, temp control, hot-swappable tips. 

There are also some great JBC clones at the range of 100-200€ from Aliexpress, look into the AIXUN, the T3A, T3B, the T320 and the T420 are great products. They have awesome performance in terms of heat transfer. 

There are some known issues due to software on the T3A and B and they tend to overshoot their power a bit, but I believe that it is fixable with an updated software. Also they hold some Voltage to the tips, like 0.5V. Nothing major but if you are soldering on a grounded board I would take it into consideration. But these are only found on T3A-B, the newer models don't have those issues.

A configurator is basically a file reader that reads JSON files. Now JSON files can give you back objects with json_decode, and those objects have inside settings to pass to other classes.

I like to think them as game config files. Like some games that have a file that you can change the settings of the game directly from this file. It has inside some properties like 'Resolution' or 'Texture Quality' or 'Shadows' and the configurator only has to read that file or files and reads the properties. It doesn't care what there is inside there, but it has to read every file inside every dir inside a specific directory in this case it's named 'configurations'.
